title: Louisiana-Style Shrimp Étouffée with Wild-Rice Pilaf
dek: Tender shrimp simmer briefly in a buttery, brick-orange Cajun gravy and surround a mound of parsley-flecked long-grain and wild-rice pilaf.
image_alt: Platter of shrimp in orange-brown étouffée gravy surrounding parsley-flecked long-grain and wild-rice pilaf
ingredients: 1 cup long-grain white rice, rinsed until the water is mostly clear
1 1/2 lb large raw shrimp, 21 to 25 count, peeled and deveined
1 medium yellow onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
1 medium green bell pepper, cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 cups low-sodium seafood or chicken stock
1 tsp hot sauce, plus more for serving
3 scallions, thinly sliced, white and green parts separated

instructions.name: Start the wild rice
instructions.text: Combine the wild rice and 1 1/2 cups chicken stock in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to the lowest simmer, cover and cook for 25 minutes. The grains will have started to split but will not yet be tender.

instructions.name: Finish the two-rice pilaf
instructions.text: Stir the rinsed white rice, remaining 1 cup chicken stock, 1 tablespoon butter and 1/4 teaspoon salt into the wild rice. Return to a simmer, cover and cook over low heat for 18 minutes. Remove from the heat, leave covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and fold in 2 tablespoons parsley. If your wild rice is unusually firm after the rest, add 2 tablespoons hot water, cover and steam over low heat for 5 minutes more.

instructions.name: Season the shrimp
instructions.text: While the pilaf cooks, pat the shrimp very dry. Toss them with 1/2 teaspoon Cajun seasoning and the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, then refrigerate while you build the gravy. Keeping the shrimp cold prevents them from overcooking before the sauce is ready.

instructions.name: Cook the butter roux
instructions.text: Melt 6 tablespoons butter in a wide 5-quart sauté pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, whisking almost constantly, until the roux is smooth and the color of peanut butter. Reduce the heat if dark specks appear; a scorched roux must be discarded.

instructions.name: Soften the Cajun trinity
instructions.text: Add the onion, bell pepper and celery to the roux. Cook for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring frequently, until the vegetables soften and the onion turns translucent. Add the garlic, tomato paste, scallion whites and remaining 1 teaspoon Cajun seasoning; cook for 2 minutes, until the paste darkens slightly.

instructions.name: Build the étouffée gravy
instructions.text: Slowly whisk in the 2 cups seafood stock, about 1/2 cup at a time, smoothing the sauce after each addition. Stir in the Worcestershire, hot sauce, bay leaf, thyme and black pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon but still flows around the rice.

instructions.name: Poach the shrimp safely
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the seasoned shrimp in one layer. Simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring once, until the shrimp are opaque, curled into loose C shapes and reach 145°F in the thickest pieces. Do not continue cooking after they form tight O shapes.

instructions.name: Brighten and adjust
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the lemon juice, half the scallion greens and all but 1 tablespoon of the remaining parsley. Taste and add salt or hot sauce only as needed. If the gravy is too thick, loosen it with hot stock 1 tablespoon at a time.

instructions.name: Plate like the photograph
instructions.text: Pack about 3/4 cup pilaf into a small bowl and invert it in the center of each warm plate. Spoon the shrimp and flowing orange-brown gravy around the rice, leaving the rice mound visible, then scatter with the reserved parsley and scallion greens.

why_it_works: Cooking the wild rice before adding white rice gives both grains enough time to become tender without turning the white rice mushy.
A carefully cooked blond-to-peanut-brown butter roux thickens the stock and supplies the nutty backbone associated with étouffée without making the sauce pasty.
Adding the shrimp only after the gravy is fully developed keeps them plump and tender, while tomato paste and the Cajun trinity create the photographed brick-orange color without cream.
swaps: Use 1 1/2 cups cooked plain long-grain rice instead of the pilaf when time is short; warm it thoroughly and omit the wild-rice cooking steps.
Crawfish tail meat can replace the shrimp ounce for ounce. Stir thawed, drained tails into the finished gravy for only 2 to 3 minutes, until they reach 145°F.
For a gluten-free gravy, replace the flour with 3 tablespoons sweet rice flour and verify that the Cajun seasoning, stock and Worcestershire sauce are gluten-free.
storage: Divide the pilaf and étouffée into separate shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Reheat the gravy gently over medium-low heat, adding a splash of stock, until it reaches 165°F; prolonged boiling will toughen the shrimp. Reheat rice with 1 tablespoon water per serving, covered, to 165°F. Freeze the gravy without shrimp for up to 2 months; freshly cook and add shrimp after thawing.
notes: Salt levels vary widely in Cajun seasoning. A salt-free blend lets the measured salt, stock and Worcestershire provide controlled seasoning.
The roux continues to darken from residual heat when the vegetables are added, so stop at peanut-butter brown rather than waiting for a dark chocolate color.
A wide pan matters: it lets the shrimp sit in a shallow layer so they cook evenly and makes it easy to judge whether the gravy flows like the photographed sauce.

faqs.q: Why did my étouffée gravy turn lumpy?
faqs.a: The stock was added too quickly or was very cold. Whisk in room-temperature or warm stock gradually, smoothing each addition before adding more. If small lumps remain, strain the gravy before returning the vegetables and adding shrimp.

faqs.q: Can I prepare shrimp étouffée ahead for guests?
faqs.a: Prepare the pilaf and gravy through the 15-minute simmer up to 1 day ahead, cool promptly and refrigerate separately. Reheat the gravy to a gentle simmer, then add raw seasoned shrimp and cook to 145°F just before serving.

faqs.q: Is étouffée supposed to be thick like gumbo?
faqs.a: It should be thicker than gumbo but looser than pot-pie filling. The finished gravy should coat a spoon and pool around the rice. Use hot stock to loosen an overly thick sauce or simmer a thin sauce a few minutes before adding the shrimp.

title: Osaka-Style Pork Okonomiyaki with Cabbage & Bonito
dek: Crisp-edged Japanese savory pancakes hide a tender cabbage-and-pork center beneath glossy okonomiyaki sauce, Kewpie mayonnaise, aonori and dancing bonito flakes.
image_alt: Two Osaka-style okonomiyaki pancakes covered with dark sauce, white mayonnaise stripes, green aonori and bonito flakes
ingredients: 12 oz green cabbage, cored and very finely shredded, about 5 packed cups
8 oz thinly sliced uncured pork belly or bacon
1/2 cup loosely packed katsuobushi bonito flakes
1/4 cup beni shoga pickled red ginger, drained, for serving

instructions.name: Mix the quick okonomiyaki sauce
instructions.text: Whisk the ketchup, Worcestershire, oyster sauce and honey in a small bowl until smooth. Transfer the mayonnaise to a squeeze bottle or snip a tiny corner from a zip-top bag so the photographed thin white stripes are easy to make.

instructions.name: Make a light batter
instructions.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Add the dashi and eggs and whisk only until no dry flour remains; a few small lumps are better than an overmixed, tough pancake.

instructions.name: Fold in the cabbage
instructions.text: Add the shredded cabbage, scallions and tenkasu to the batter. Fold with a flexible spatula until every strand is lightly coated. The mixture should look mostly like cabbage held together by a thin batter, not pourable pancake batter.

instructions.name: Shape the first pancake
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch nonstick or well-seasoned cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Spoon half the cabbage mixture into the skillet and shape it into an even 7-inch round about 1 inch thick. Do not press it flat. Arrange half the pork slices in one layer across the top.

instructions.name: Cook the first side
instructions.text: Cover and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, until the underside is deeply golden and the cabbage begins to soften. Slide a wide spatula underneath to confirm the pancake releases cleanly before attempting to flip.

instructions.name: Flip and cook the pork side
instructions.text: Set a dinner plate over the skillet, invert the pancake onto it, then slide it back into the skillet pork-side down. Cover and cook for 6 to 7 minutes. Uncover and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until the pork is browned and reaches at least 145°F and the center of the pancake feels set rather than wet.

instructions.name: Repeat without crowding
instructions.text: Transfer the first pancake to a warm plate. Wipe out any dark crumbs, add the remaining tablespoon oil and repeat with the remaining cabbage mixture and pork. Keep the first pancake warm in a 200°F oven if desired.

instructions.name: Glaze and garnish
instructions.text: Brush each hot pancake generously with okonomiyaki sauce. Pipe mayonnaise in narrow parallel stripes, sprinkle with aonori and finish with bonito flakes so the heat makes them flutter. Serve the pickled ginger alongside, matching the photographed glossy brown, white and green finish.

instructions.name: Slice and serve
instructions.text: Cut each pancake into four wedges and serve two wedges per person while the edges are crisp. Provide extra sauce and pickled ginger at the table rather than soaking the cut surfaces in advance.

why_it_works: Finely shredded cabbage steams inside the covered pancake while a restrained amount of batter binds it, producing a tender center rather than a dense floury cake.
Starting pork-side up lets the cabbage base set firmly enough to flip; the pork then renders directly against the pan and flavors the pancake as it finishes.
Sweet-tangy sauce, rich mayonnaise, savory bonito and mineral aonori create the characteristic layered finish visible in the photograph.
swaps: Replace pork belly with 8 ounces peeled raw shrimp chopped into 1/2-inch pieces. Fold them into the batter and cook until every piece reaches 145°F.
If Kewpie mayonnaise is unavailable, stir 1 teaspoon rice vinegar and 1/2 teaspoon sugar into 1/3 cup regular mayonnaise.
For a vegetarian version, omit the pork, oyster sauce and bonito. Add 6 ounces thinly sliced shiitake mushrooms to the cabbage and use vegetarian Worcestershire plus hoisin in place of oyster sauce.
storage: Cool ungarnished pancakes and refrigerate in a shallow airtight container within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Reheat on a lightly oiled skillet over medium-low for 4 to 5 minutes per side, or in a 375°F oven for 10 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F. Add sauce, mayonnaise, aonori and bonito only after reheating. Freeze parchment-separated, ungarnished pancakes for up to 1 month.
notes: A mandoline produces the fine, even cabbage shreds that soften on schedule, but use its hand guard and stop before the cabbage becomes too small to hold safely.
Tenkasu adds small crisp pockets but is optional; do not replace it with a large amount of panko, which absorbs moisture and makes the center bready.
Two medium pancakes are much easier to flip and cook through than one oversized pancake, and they match the two-pancake presentation in the photograph.

faqs.q: Why did my okonomiyaki fall apart when I flipped it?
faqs.a: The first side had not formed a firm crust or the cabbage was too coarsely cut. Keep the pancake near 7 inches, cook it covered for the full 6 to 7 minutes and verify that a wide spatula can lift the whole base before flipping with a plate.

faqs.q: Can I make okonomiyaki batter ahead?
faqs.a: Whisk the flour batter and refrigerate it for up to 8 hours, but fold in cabbage, scallions and tenkasu immediately before cooking. Salted batter pulls water from cabbage and becomes thin if it sits assembled.

faqs.q: What can I use if I cannot find dashi, aonori or bonito flakes?
faqs.a: Use cool water plus 1 teaspoon soy sauce for the dashi, finely crumbled nori for aonori and omit bonito if necessary. The pancake will still work, though the specialty ingredients provide the most recognizable Japanese flavor.

title: Vanilla-Bean Panna Cotta with Fresh Berries & Honey
dek: A softly set Italian cream dessert unmolds into elegant fluted rounds, topped with red and golden raspberries, blackberries and a glossy lemon-honey drizzle.
image_alt: Fluted white panna cotta topped with golden and red raspberries and blackberries in a clear honey drizzle
ingredients: 2 1/4 tsp unflavored powdered gelatin, one 1/4-ounce packet
1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise and seeds scraped, or 2 tsp vanilla bean paste
1 tsp neutral oil, for the molds
3 oz fresh golden raspberries or additional red raspberries

instructions.name: Prepare the molds
instructions.text: Lightly wipe six 6-ounce fluted molds or ramekins with the neutral oil, then remove every visible puddle with a paper towel. Arrange the molds on a small rimmed tray that fits level in the refrigerator.

instructions.name: Bloom the gelatin
instructions.text: Pour 1/2 cup of the cold milk into a medium heat-safe bowl and sprinkle the gelatin evenly over the surface. Leave undisturbed for 5 to 10 minutes, until the gelatin is swollen and no dry islands remain. Stirring too early encourages stubborn clumps.

instructions.name: Infuse the cream
instructions.text: Combine the heavy cream, remaining 1/2 cup milk, sugar, vanilla seeds and pod, and salt in a 2-quart saucepan. Heat over medium-low, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the mixture reaches 170 to 180°F with steam rising around the edge. Do not boil.

instructions.name: Dissolve and strain
instructions.text: Remove and discard the vanilla pod. Pour one-third of the hot cream over the bloomed gelatin and whisk until completely clear and smooth, then whisk in the remaining cream. Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer into a clean pitcher to catch any undissolved gelatin.

instructions.name: Fill without foam
instructions.text: Let the mixture stand for 5 minutes, then skim bubbles from the surface. Divide evenly among the prepared molds, about 2/3 cup each. Pop remaining surface bubbles with the tip of a clean knife so the unmolded tops look smooth.

instructions.name: Chill until softly set
instructions.text: Cover the tray without touching the surfaces and refrigerate for at least 4 hours and up to 2 days. The panna cotta is ready when it holds still at the edge but gives a delicate wobble in the center. Keep it at 40°F or colder.

instructions.name: Make the honey drizzle
instructions.text: Warm the honey, lemon juice and lemon zest in a small saucepan or microwave-safe cup just until fluid, about 30 seconds. Cool completely. Gently rinse the berries, drain well and pat dry so they do not weep onto the cream.

instructions.name: Release each panna cotta
instructions.text: Dip one mold into warm—not hot—water for 5 seconds, keeping water below the rim. Dry the outside, run a thin knife just around the top 1/4 inch and invert onto a chilled plate. If it does not release, repeat the warm-water dip for 2 seconds; excess heat melts the edges.

instructions.name: Match the berry presentation
instructions.text: Top each fluted white panna cotta with red and golden raspberries and blackberries. Spoon the cooled honey drizzle over the fruit and around the base, leaving most of the pale cream visible, and serve immediately.

why_it_works: Blooming gelatin in cold milk hydrates every granule before heat is introduced, preventing rubbery flecks and helping the dessert set evenly.
A roughly three-to-one dairy-to-gelatin balance creates enough structure to unmold while preserving the delicate wobble expected from panna cotta.
Vanilla, rich cream, tart berries and lemon-brightened honey create contrast without a cooked compote that would hide the fresh-fruit presentation shown in the photograph.
swaps: Use six straight-sided ramekins and serve the panna cotta in the dishes if you prefer to skip unmolding; no oil is needed in that case.
Replace up to 1 cup heavy cream with full-fat canned coconut milk for a subtle coconut note, but keep the whole milk and gelatin quantities unchanged for a reliable set.
Strawberries or blueberries can replace either raspberry variety. Keep the total fruit near 15 ounces and cut strawberries into bite-size pieces only after drying them.
storage: Cover molds individually and refrigerate at 40°F or colder for up to 3 days. Store washed berries and cooled honey drizzle separately, then unmold and garnish only when serving. Panna cotta should not be frozen because thawing damages its smooth gel structure. Discard portions left at room temperature longer than 2 hours.
notes: Measure powdered gelatin with a level teaspoon or use one sealed 1/4-ounce packet; even a small excess can make the panna cotta bouncy instead of tender.
Boiling weakens gelatin and can give cream a cooked flavor. Stop heating as soon as the sugar dissolves and the mixture reaches 170 to 180°F.
Golden raspberries match the photographed garnish but are optional and seasonal; additional red raspberries preserve the flavor and structure.

faqs.q: Why did my panna cotta fail to set?
faqs.a: The gelatin may not have bloomed fully, the mixture may have boiled or the dessert may not have chilled long enough. Use a fresh 1/4-ounce packet, bloom it for at least 5 minutes, keep the cream below a boil and allow a full 4 hours in a refrigerator at 40°F or colder.

faqs.q: How do I unmold panna cotta without melting it?
faqs.a: Use warm water for only 5 seconds, dry the mold and loosen only the top edge with a thin knife. Invert and give one firm downward shake. Repeat with a 2-second dip rather than leaving the mold submerged longer.

faqs.q: Can panna cotta be made two days ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Keep it covered in the molds for up to 2 days, with berries and drizzle stored separately. Unmold while cold and garnish immediately before serving so the fruit stays fresh and the surface remains clean.
